label: rem:eightfold-open-problems
title: Open problems
html:
This section collects the open problems identified during the construction of this chapter, each stated with a falsifiable test.

Consolidated ledger. Every structural ingredient the chapter uses, with its tier (the root-system section). Items marked open name the missing object precisely. The "Where" column points to the numbered items below by name rather than by number, so that reordering the list cannot silently break the pointers.

Ingredient Status Where
H_3(q) has Coxeter type A_2; W(A_2) \cong S_3 standard, and true by construction (B_n has type A_{n-1}) A_2 from three strands
A_2 Cartan datum is independent of q under Drinfeld--Jimbo quantisation standard (Lusztig/Kashiwara), cited and not proved here q-deformation
Serre exponent; root-angle ratio; the "two 2s" separation (the Serre coefficient [2]_q moves with q while the Cartan datum does not) proved q-deformation
Root/weight lattices, Weyl group, Kazhdan–Lusztig multiplicities are q-independent standard (Drinfeld–Jimbo), not proved here q-deformation
Quantum Schur–Weyl duality \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_N) \leftrightarrow H_n(q) standard [jimbo1986]; the duality itself is not proved here, only its row-cap consequence Schur–Weyl
\mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1}; \dim \mathrm{Sym}^3(W_3^*) = \binom{5}{3} = 10; quantum [3]_q^3 = (q^2 + q^{-2})[5]_q + 2[2]_q[4]_q + 1; weight tables traceless/scalar vector-space split, polynomial-module dimension 10 \neq 4, and generic-q quantum dimension balance proved; \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} equivariance and applicability conditional on N = 3 meson octet, decuplet
N = 2 cannot host the eightfold-way decomposition standard, with a proved arithmetic instance: \dim V_{(1^3)} is taken to be \binom{N}{3}, and \binom{N}{3} = 0 \iff N < 3 is proved. The hook-content formula and the row cap \ell(\lambda) \le N are cited, not proved — same caveat as the q-deformation row Schur–Weyl
\dim V = N = 3 for the flavour fundamental open: framework supplies \dim V = 2; no q raises the row cap. The obstruction is proved; the construction is missing item The N = 3 problem
No object of the single-fibre category reaches \dim W = 3 through the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate proved, and at object level rather than only for irreducible summands: the Frobenius--Schur count forces a passing W to be a sum of pairwise distinct even-dimensional irreps, so \dim W is even, and 3 is odd item The N = 3 problem
Inequivalent fibre functors of the single-fibre category standard [bichon2003]: they exist at every dimension n \ge 2 and are real at q_0; and proved that none of them supplies a one-dimensional summand of V^{\otimes 3} --- the spin-0 object is absent by Clebsch--Gordan parity, so the fusion rules, which every fibre functor preserves, exclude \mathbf{10} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1} at every n item The N = 3 problem
Writhe-to-isospin map w \mapsto I_3 on the nucleon doublet derived, scale-free, no fitted parameters, for the writhe of the inter-nucleon arc; the ruled nucleon word has writhe 0 for both nucleons flavour charges
Hypercharge Y and split-bundle F = V_2 \oplus W_3^* coupling conditionally coupled to N = 3: single-fibre writhe map falsified (p, n share Y = +1); on F = V_2 \oplus W_3^* (z_3 = q^3/[3]_q), tracelessness 2y_2 + 3y_3 = 0 \iff y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3}y_2 is proved (fixing doublet y_2 + y_3 = +\tfrac{1}{3}, Killing Weinberg ratio 3/8, and separating \bar u = -\tfrac{2}{3} from d = -\tfrac{1}{3}); open: categorical construction of W_3 flavour charges, item Hypercharge Y
Baryon octet weight degeneracy and H_3(q) S^{(2,1)} diquark split proved (exclusion + operator split), open (scale): weight-only formulas give m_\Lambda = m_{\Sigma^0} (excluded at 77\;\mathrm{MeV}), while internal S^{(2,1)} diquark projectors P_\Lambda, P_{\Sigma^0} give \mathrm{tr}(P_\Lambda V^3) - \mathrm{tr}(P_{\Sigma^0} V^3) = (q - q^{-1})^3(q^2 + q^{-2})[3]_q/[2]_q \neq 0 (31.5\;\mathrm{MeV} at q_0 vs empirical 77.0\;\mathrm{MeV}) baryon octet
Ordered 3-strand gluon clasp \beta_{\mathrm{clasp}}(n_1, n_2) on neutral mesons proved (invariants), open (absolute mass scale): \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) trace 2n_1n_2 + n_1 + n_2 + 3 \ge 27 > 2 across \{3,5,7\}^2, separating \bar D^0 = (-5,+3) from K^0 = (+3,-5) in both z_2 and z_3 Markov traces meson mass splitting, dictionary supplement
\mathrm{PSL}(2,7) \cong \mathrm{GL}(3,\mathbb{F}_2), order 168, irreps \{1,3,\bar 3,6,7,8\} standard; machine-verified numerically colour from G_2
S_4 bridge: transitive on local Fano lines verified numerically colour from G_2
The S_4 bridge selects the Klein quartic refuted (verified by exact computation), and not narrowly: the S_4-invariant quartics form a pencil, so infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic genus-3 curves admit S_4 (Fermat is the member t = 0 of the pencil, t being the pencil parameter, not a partition). The datum has essentially no separating power colour from G_2
Bring \to Klein-quartic genus degeneration excluded under its own three premises (scope-(b)): the pinch supplies an S_4-stable pair of marked points, and S_4 has no orbit of size \le 2 on \mathbb{P}^2, since the 3-dimensional representation and its restriction to A_4 are both absolutely irreducible. No smooth plane quartic carries such a pair, and Klein is not hyperelliptic. Rescue requires explicitly dropping one premise: hyperelliptic target, multi-node/separating pinch, or non-faithful S_4 colour from G_2
Octonionic \mathbf{3} not excluded by the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate literature decomposition: at dimension three, passing the gate forces a complex-type summand (proved), and that the Günaydin--Gürsey triple is complex type is the cited \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}}-irreducibility input, not a proved one Schur–Weyl
The octonion algebra \mathbb{O} and G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}) established: definition in the colour-algebra section, with \mathrm{Der}(\mathbb{O}) = \mathfrak{g}_2 ([baez2002]) and the Baez-convention multiplication definition
Continuous G_2 completion (S^6 = G_2/\mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}}) open: the continuous Lie group G_2 is not constructed here — an infrastructure gap, not a structural one item Continuous G_2 completion
Flavour vs. colour (\mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} vs. \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}}) open: whether same, different, or groupoid-dual item Flavour versus colour separation
Gell-Mann–Okubo has no discriminating power proved: 4m_K^2 - 3m_\eta^2 - m_\pi^2 = 0 identically for any first-order octet breaking meson mass splitting
Meson mass splitting; the GMO deviation partially resolved (sign), open (magnitude): rational quantum Casimir gives (4M_K - 3M_\eta - M_\pi)/(M_\pi - M_\eta) = -((q-1)/(q+1))^2 (proved, matching both meson + and baryon - signs at q_0), but accounts for only 1.21\% of the 6.43\% meson deviation; \eta--\eta' mixing remains open meson mass splitting, item The Gell-Mann--Okubo deviation
Spin–flavour–colour selection of the Young symmetriser open: decuplet identification currently matches dimensions and weights only item Spin--flavour--colour selection rule
Truncation ("freeze-out") mechanism open: heuristic, no derivation item Truncation mechanism
Three generations open: not addressed here item Three generations

The chapter cannot do without N = 3: the meson octet, the baryon multiplets, and every quark row of the dictionary are conditional on a three-dimensional partner, which is unavailable from a single fibre. As shown in the Standard Model appendix and in the flavour-charges remark, hypercharge is coupled to that same missing partner: on the split bundle F = V_2 \oplus W_3^* (z_3 = q^3/[3]_q), tracelessness forces y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3}y_2 with no free parameter, whereas without W_3^* the chapter reproduces I_3 alone and cannot close the Gell-Mann--Nishijima relation.

  1. The N = 3 problem. Schur--Weyl duality [jimbo1986] (Proposition) requires the fundamental representation to be 3-dimensional. The single-fibre tower has \dim V = 2 (the standard single-fibre construction; the Descartes condition \chi(\mathcal{A}) = -6 is compatible with but does not uniquely force N = 2). That N = 2 cannot host the decomposition is now proved (the alternating channel \binom{N}{3} vanishes iff N < 3, and the decuplet dimension forces N = 3) --- so the obstruction is settled and only the construction is missing. Open: construct a three-dimensional object W in the multi-fibre groupoid whose symmetric square \mathrm{Sym}^2(W) is irreducible (no singlet). The octonion G_2 route supplies a colour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} candidate that the gate does not exclude --- not excluded rather than passes, since the singlet count 0 that would make it pass is the cited \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}}-irreducibility input and not a proved one (see the ledger). Whether it yields flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} is untested.

    What such a construction must supply is now a theorem, and it is one property rather than a list. Putting the two halves together: a three-dimensional object passing the gate must contain a complex-type irrep , and a category all of whose irreps are self-dual contains none — which is precisely the single-fibre case, since every \mathrm{SU}(2) irrep is self-dual. So the property a groupoid construction must exhibit is exactly the property one fibre lacks: non-self-duality. This yields a screening test : a candidate whose three-dimensional object is isomorphic to its own dual is dead, and can be discarded before its \mathrm{Sym}^2 decomposition is computed. It does not construct anything — Route A stays open — but it replaces "more structure" with a single checkable condition.

    The same condition is reachable from the row cap, independently. The Descartes characteristic \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 forces \mathrm{SU}(2), hence \dim V = 2, hence partitions of at most two rows, so the (1^3) block drops at n = 3 and a three-dimensional object cannot be a tensor power of the single fibre. That argument reaches non-self-duality without the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate and without the Frobenius--Schur trichotomy, as the gate-and-trichotomy argument reaches it without the Euler characteristic and without Schur--Weyl. A third route reaches the same negative from a different direction again: N \neq 3 follows from non-degeneracy of the fibre's volume form (\Lambda^2 V \cong \mathbf{1} forces N = 2), without the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate, the row cap or the Euler characteristic.

    The three are not three votes on one proposition, and the difference is what matters here. The row-cap and volume-form arguments bound the fibre: they say N = 2, so one fibre cannot supply a three-dimensional object. The gate-and-trichotomy argument bounds any candidate: it says which property a candidate must have, and so yields a test that can be applied to an object nobody has built yet. The negative is now over-determined; the screen is what is additive.

    That the search is confined to the groupoid level is now a theorem, not an extrapolation. The parity criterion decides the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate for a single irreducible summand, and a three-dimensional W need not be irreducible --- W = V_{1/2} \oplus V_0 has dimension 3, sits in the tensor category generated by the fibre, and is not an irrep, so that criterion does not reach it. The multiplicity form closes the case: counting singlets by Frobenius--Schur type, a passing W must be a sum of pairwise distinct even-dimensional irreps, hence \dim W is even. Since 3 is odd, no three-dimensional object of the single-fibre category passes the gate, reducible or not. Any N = 3 must therefore come from genuinely multi-fibre structure --- which is what the route above asserts, now with a proved invariant behind it (a scope-(b) exclusion, the invariant being the Frobenius--Schur indicator (-1)^{2j}). Even dimension is necessary, not sufficient: V_{1/2}^{\oplus 2} has dimension 4 and fails the gate too, so the parity invariant prunes candidates rather than characterising them. The octonionic candidate is no counterexample to this: it is not an object of the single-fibre category at all, arising instead from G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}), which is precisely why the parity exclusion leaves it standing.

    The mechanism behind that escape is now proved rather than asserted, and it is worth stating because it bounds how far the exclusion reaches. The parity argument runs through self-duality: every \mathrm{SU}(2) irrep satisfies V^* \cong V, so the cross terms V_i \otimes V_j contribute no singlet and the survivors are forced to be distinct even-dimensional irreps. A complex-type representation (\mathrm{FS} = 0, \mathbf{3} \not\cong \bar{\mathbf{3}}) pairs to a singlet only against its conjugate, so one whose conjugate is absent from the object passes the gate at any dimension, odd included --- and such an object is exhibited at dimension exactly 3. So the even-dimension exclusion above is a scope-(b) exclusion within the self-dual sector and is silent, not negative, outside it. This is the same non-self-duality that the colour construction already identifies as what the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate consumes.

    Nor is the fibre functor the missing knob. The single-fibre category admits fibre functors of every dimension n \ge 2 [bichon2003]: for E \in \mathrm{GL}_n with \mathrm{tr}(E^{-1}E^{t}) = -q - q^{-1} the comodule category of the bilinear-form quantum group B(E) is monoidally equivalent to that of \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SL}_2), and such E exist over \mathbb{R} at q_0 for every n \ge 3. So a three-dimensional image of V is available. It does not help, because a fibre functor is monoidal and therefore preserves the Clebsch--Gordan rule: under a three-dimensional fibre functor V^{\otimes 3} \cong V_{3/2} \oplus V_{1/2} \oplus V_{1/2} has dimensions 21 + 3 + 3, and under a fibre functor of any dimension the spin-0 summand the decomposition \mathbf{10} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1} requires is absent from V^{\otimes 3} by parity . Dimension is a property of the fibre functor; the multiplet structure is a property of the category. This closes the single-fibre reading of Route A --- the question does the category admit inequivalent fibre functors? is answered affirmatively and turns out not to bear on N = 3 --- and relocates the missing object to the category itself: an object W with \Lambda^3 W \neq 0, which the categorical volume constraint (Definition, condition 5) forbids for the fundamental.

  2. Hypercharge Y. The writhe-to-isospin map w \mapsto I_3 is derived. The hypercharge Y is not: the writhe map is falsified as a Y assignment (proton and neutron share Y = +1 while their writhes differ). Open: identify a second crossing invariant independent of the writhe. Battery (exploratory, not wired): of 10{,}000 helon-style assignments, 4 survive --- but that ratio carries no corroboration, and is not a 2500\!:\!1 filter. It is proved that the spectrum battery is exactly T = 3Q (the -2I_3 common to candidate and target cancels, leaving the defining equation of Q_{\mathrm{twist}}, not a test of it); the nucleon check is entailed by charge additivity and states one condition twice; and the \mathbb{Z}_6 condition never sees the assignment, so it filters nothing. Each flavour is thus filtered independently by one linear equation, and 4 = 1 \times 2 \times 2 \times 1 counts multisets with totals 3Q = (2,-1,0,-3) --- the "uniquely determined" u and electron multisets being the two totals that admit a single multiset. A parameter-free repair using the canonical ribbon twist (Q = c(\lambda)/3, c the content sum) was tested and fails: at n = 3 it gives the integer charges \{+1,0,-1\}, and no n \le 8 yields both quark charges ; scope-(a) for that reading only. The derivation gap is therefore the entire content: whether the twist multisets are forced by the categorical braid words (not just consistent with them) is the open content of the hypercharge conjecture, and nothing else in the battery constrains anything. In the split-bundle framing F = V_2 \oplus W_3^* (z_3 = q^3/[3]_q) of the Standard Model appendix and the flavour-charges remark, tracelessness of \mathrm{diag}(y_2, y_2, y_3, y_3, y_3) forces y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3}y_2, pinning the exterior-pair doublet hypercharge y_2 + y_3 = +\tfrac{1}{3} at y_2 = 1 with Killing Weinberg ratio 3/8, and separating \bar u (-\tfrac{2}{3}) from d (-\tfrac{1}{3}) despite their shared crossing sign -1. Hypercharge is thus reduced conditionally to the same missing object as item 1: constructing W_3 in the multi-fibre groupoid.

  3. Continuous G_2 completion. The discrete skeleton of \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} \subset G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}) is verified (\mathrm{GL}(3, \mathbb{F}_2) \cong \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) Fano symmetry of the associator). The continuous Lie-group completion --- specifically the coset S^6 = G_2/\mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} --- not constructed here: the continuous Lie group G_2 is not available. This is an infrastructure obstruction, not a structural one.

  4. Flavour versus colour separation. The octonionic \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} is colour. The eightfold-way classification requires flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}. Whether these are the same, different, or related by a groupoid-level duality is open, and the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate cannot settle it.

    In particular the gate does not show that the two cannot both come from the same construction. That it excludes the icosahedral triple T_1 while the G_2 route passes compares two different objects and establishes only that those two differ, not that one construction cannot supply both roles. (The T_1 comparison is in the Schur--Weyl proposition, where it is stated as not excluded on a literature decomposition.)

    The failure is structural, not a repairable gap in the inference. It is proved that at dimension three, passing the gate is equivalent to carrying a complex-type irrep. Any two three-dimensional objects that both pass are therefore both complex type, and the gate has returned the same verdict for each --- two distinct such objects are exhibited. A flavour triple and a colour triple that each pass are, to this gate, indistinguishable.

    What the gate does establish is a class exclusion: no real or quaternionic construction reaches dimension three through it, so T_1's failure is a consequence of its Frobenius--Schur type and not a fact about the icosahedron. Whatever separates flavour from colour lies elsewhere --- as it does for the \mathbb{Z}/3 grading, which is likewise shown to be blind to the identification.

    The two blindnesses are one blindness. Both gates read only object-level data --- a dimension, a Frobenius--Schur type, a triality class --- and on that data the two triples coincide: the colour triple is the \mathbb{C}^3 of \mathrm{Im}(\mathbb{O}) = \mathbb{R}\oplus\mathbb{C}^3, of complex dimension (7-1)/2 = 3; the flavour triple is the fundamental with Dynkin label (1,0), of Weyl dimension 2\cdot 1\cdot 3/2 = 3; both are complex type with triality 1. This is a class exclusion, and a proved one --- no gate reading only object data separates them, so there is no third such gate to look for. This is scope-(b), with the invariant named: equal data, equal verdict.

    Where a discriminator can live is item 7 below, not a further invariant of the object. The obstruction lifts as soon as a gate may also read which Young-symmetry channel of V^{\otimes 3} carries the physical state: colour occupies the totally antisymmetric channel \lambda = (1^3), flavour the symmetric \lambda = (3) for the decuplet and the mixed \lambda = (2,1) for the octet. These are distinct S_3-irreps, and a gate is exhibited that tells them apart. Item 7 already names this data, in the form "colour antisymmetric and spin symmetric force flavour symmetric"; items 4 and 7 are the same question seen from two sides.

    This locates the discriminator; it does not establish one. The channel assignment is an input, and item 7 records that the chapter derives neither the spin factor nor the colour antisymmetry that would supply it. What is settled is the negative half --- and the negative half is what redirects the search.

  5. Truncation mechanism. Why does the observable-scale symmetry reduce to a finite-dimensional Lie group rather than the full groupoid symmetry? Root-of-unity truncation is a candidate (T4), but no derivation of the specific root of unity from QOU axioms exists.

  6. Three generations. The A_2 root system and eightfold-way classification are generation-independent. Why there are exactly three generations of fermions is a separate open problem (T6), not addressed here.

  7. Spin--flavour--colour selection rule. The identification \lambda = (3) \leftrightarrow decuplet, \lambda = (2,1) \leftrightarrow octet (Proposition) currently matches dimensions and weights only. What physically forces the symmetric flavour channel for the spin-3/2 decuplet is antisymmetry of the total wavefunction once colour is included --- colour antisymmetric and spin symmetric force flavour symmetric. This chapter derives neither the spin factor nor the colour antisymmetry. Open: produce the spin degree of freedom and the colour-antisymmetry constraint from the braid structure, and show that together they determine the Young symmetriser. Compatibility with it is what the chapter currently establishes.

    This item is where item 4's discriminator lives. Item 4 asks what separates flavour from colour and shows that no invariant of the object can; the Young-symmetry channel named here is data about the role, and a gate is exhibited that reads it and does separate them. So deriving the colour-antisymmetry constraint would settle more than the selection rule --- it would supply the one input item 4 is missing.

  8. The Gell-Mann--Okubo deviation. The relation 4m_K^2 = 3m_\eta^2 + m_\pi^2 is not a target for derivation: it holds identically for any first-order octet breaking, whatever the mechanism, as proved in the meson mass-splitting remark. Reproducing it would therefore be no evidence for the framework. An unconstrained second-order polynomial in (I(I+1), Y) surjects onto every scalar residual and likewise carries no separating power. Replacing the classical Casimir by the parameter-free rational quantum Casimir d_q(I, Y) = [I]_q[I+1]_q - [Y/2]_q^2 [kleinkreisler1996] yields the (a,b,c)-free bar-even ratio (4M_K - 3M_\eta - M_\pi)/(M_\pi - M_\eta) = -((q - 1)/(q + 1))^2, equal to -2.7168 \times 10^{-3} at q_0. This predicts the observed signs on both the pseudoscalar meson octet (+) and the baryon octet (-) without free parameters, while accounting for only 1.21\% of the 6.43\% isospin-averaged meson deviation and 0.82\% of the -0.57\% baryon deviation. Open: the remaining \approx 6.3\% meson residual, dominated by \eta--\eta' singlet mixing and higher-order \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} breaking. The former \approx 3.3\% comparison against \dim_q(\text{adjoint}) remains withdrawn as a category error (a dimension is not a mass splitting).

  9. Ocneanu/Markov trace parameter. The Markov trace \tau on H_n(q) involves a second parameter z (the trace parameter). In QOU, q is the substrate parameter (observed at the point of observation as q_0, not derived from Bring topology). Along the Wenzl family z_r = q^r/[r]_q, a fibre of quantum dimension [r]_q pins z = z_r with nothing left to choose: V_2 fixes z_2 = q^3/(q^2+1) and a rank-3 partner W_3^* fixes z_3 = q^3/[3]_q = q^5/(q^4+q^2+1). The two parameters satisfy z_2(q) - z_3(q) = q^3 / ((q^2+1)(q^4+q^2+1)) \neq 0 (0.1634 at q_0) and induce non-proportional Ocneanu weight vectors on H_3(q) (w_{(1^3)}(q, z_2) = 0 whereas w_{(1^3)}(q, z_3) = [3]_q^{-3} \neq 0). Open: constructing the categorical rank-3 object W_3 that instantiates the r = 3 level (T3f).
